iterations.theme: Analysis of Dinamo's defeat at Poljud: poor lineup, coach Kovačević, transfer window and refereeing

sections.subtitle: Derby from the Edge of the European Union: a podcast recorded from England
sections.screenshot_description: Denis and Profa in a hotel room in England, with a conversation about the trip and the match at the stadium
sections.content:
The episode of the 8_24 podcast begins in unusual circumstances. Profa admits in the introduction that it is not easy to record outside the European Union, and it is even harder after a defeat in the derby. He adds that the result from Poljud hit them seriously, although they spent nice days in England.

Denis explains why they are watching Dinamo's derby from a hotel room, and not from Poljud or from the studio. According to his words, they had an opportunity that comes once in a lifetime, maybe more than once, to be guests of their former coach. Therefore they accepted it with both hands.

Denis describes what they have already managed to see in England:

- the match of Hull and Everton, with a note that the locals corrected them about the pronunciation of the club's name,
- a training session that reminded him of a day "from a fairy tale",
- the match of Manchester and Tottenham on the day of recording,
- the derby of Dinamo and Hajduk, which they watched in the hotel before that.

Profa asks jokingly whether the match at the "Theatre of Dreams" eased the pain of the defeat. Denis answers that the match was not especially good quality. Still, the whole atmosphere of English football delighted him. He says he saw why people praise the English atmosphere so much. In the second half he mentions a red card and two goals. He thinks viewers will still be more interested in talking about Dinamo.

Profa then greets friends Tonči and Luka and thanks them for the greeting at the end of their video. He adds that, thanks to a combination of work and a visit in England, they temporarily "made themselves English".

sections.subtitle: A Hundred Alibis, and None Holds: Denis Does Not Look for Excuses
sections.screenshot_description: Denis explains that Hajduk deserved to win and that Dinamo was poorly set up
sections.content:
Profa introduces the topic with a story about Kobe Bryant's interview after a lost final. The basketball player then said he could find a hundred alibis, but that he would not use any. Profa then lists Dinamo's possible excuses: Mišić was not there, Stojković was not fully healthy, the pitch was bad, and Hajduk very probably should have remained with a player fewer. He asks Denis whether any of that consoles him and whether it is an alibi.

Denis answers briefly: **he would have no alibis**. He thinks Hajduk was better and deserved to win. The refereeing and disputed situations will be a subject of discussion, but he does not see them as the cause of the defeat. According to him, the cause is Dinamo's poor play and generally poor setup, and especially a problematic starting lineup.

In this vivid way he describes what he would do if he were Dinamo's coach or director:

- he would print on the nicest printer pictures of all eleven Hajduk players and hang them in the dressing room,
- he would tell the players that they were not just beaten, but beaten up and outplayed,
- he would frame Bamba's picture and put it in front of the whole defence, with a message that he dominated against them.

Denis stresses that the most devastating thing is that Dinamo, according to his assessment, has 10 or 10 and a half better players than Hajduk's 11. He judges that Dinamo's squad on paper is twice as good. Despite that, Hajduk won without a "bunker" and without a lucky deflection. Dinamo played a good part of the match in a low or mid block and did not show anything that is expected of it.

sections.subtitle: Divorce Without a Culprit: Dinamo Needs Shock Therapy
sections.screenshot_description: Denis compares the relationship between the coach and the club to a couple whose love has disappeared
sections.content:
Denis thinks the derby result is part of a worrying run. He lists the big matches that Dinamo lost this year: Osijek and Viking, with a note that Dinamo has "luckily" kept the match with Rijeka, which it has not yet played. In the conversation Profa recalls that Dinamo has achieved only three wins in the last nine matches.

Denis explains the problem with a comparison to family friends, a married couple who divorced. He says they are great people, but the energy and love were lost. Although individually excellent, together they could no longer go on. He sees the same in Dinamo: love and energy can be born again, but the current situation with the coaching staff and the squad is not compatible with the club's expectations and its goals.

Denis concludes that the team needs **shock therapy**. He wonders whether it can pull it out of itself before Anderlecht. He emphasizes that the people may still be good, but not necessarily together. He thinks this is the "last chance" and questions the sense of insisting on what does not work from match to match.

sections.subtitle: Three Figures That Did Not Click: Kovačević and Stojković's Readiness
sections.screenshot_description: Denis analyzes Kovačević's substitutions in the 60th minute and Stojković's role
sections.content:
Denis says that coach Kovačević in the derby "took responsibility into his own hands". He decided to make three substitutions in the 60th minute, whereby, according to Denis, he himself showed that he missed with everything he had conceived for the match.

About Stojković, Denis does not want to speak of a miss. He recalls that the player himself said that on Friday he had only started to train, so realistically he was not ready. Profa notes that on Tuesday he was a star, but Denis holds to what Kovačević said in Cres and believes that it is true. If the player really trained only from Friday, there would not be too many reasons for him to play, let alone on a soft, muddy pitch. Denis would not have brought him in, because the match was without rhythm.

Profa also mentions that quite a few people reproached Stojković's coming on against Vukovar. Denis adds that not even there would he risk it, given the pitch. If the player is completely healthy, says Profa, then he should not be spared. Denis admits that this did not have too much logic for him. Maybe the coach wanted to give the player rhythm.

Denis concludes that what Dinamo plays looks like nothing. He emphasizes that the match against Anderlecht practically decides: if Dinamo does not win, it will be almost at the exit door of the Europa League.

sections.subtitle: Downward Trajectory: European Exams Kovačević Did Not Pass
sections.screenshot_description: Denis lists European failures from last season to Hapoel and Viking
sections.content:
Denis admits that Kovačević as Dinamo's coach achieved a good result. However, he claims that precisely where Dinamo needed to make a breakthrough, in Europe, he failed every exam. He starts from last season. Dinamo then entered among the 24 teams in the Europa League, but Denis warns that even that cannot be fairly defended. He mentions the match in Belgium, in which Dinamo could have gone through, and a very bad match in Zagreb. This season in Europe he already sees a failure that has been made and that can be even bigger if Dinamo does not enter among the 24 teams, which does not seem at all certain to him.

Profa throws in the argument that Kovačević can defend himself by the fact that the club openly communicated that the Europa League is the goal. But Profa notes that, because of last year's success, Dinamo was considered a favourite and had a nice path towards the Champions League. Denis responds that the trend is downward. Against Tun, Dinamo went through on God's luck, with a red card and a reversed situation, and in neither of the two matches was it better than a very modest team. Against Viking it was bad. The match with Hapoel Denis describes as the luckiest for Kovačević in the whole tenure, regardless of the heavy defeats against Celta and Lille.

Profa recalls that Dinamo had a heavy "big slap" from Osijek, then a catastrophic level of play against Hapoel and harder wins against Lokomotiva, partly because of red cards. He judges that people were not so angry only because of the three-week break between matches. Denis adds that against Hapoel Dinamo did not look like a team that has some justification, because each of them dominated, and yet it looked bad.

sections.subtitle: Bad Energy Springs from the Top: Transfer Window, Management and Zvonimir Boban
sections.screenshot_description: Denis criticizes the transfer window and the moves of Dinamo's management
sections.content:
Profa asks how much the first team and the play were actually rehearsed. Denis thinks it is logical to rehearse for about ten days and that for a week the idea with which one is going must be known. He does not understand how Galešić plays alongside Dominguez and why other players, who in his opinion deserved a chance, do not take part. As an example he cites a lad who is perhaps the best defensive player this season, and does not get a chance. He stresses that there are more examples of players toward whom the club has sinned.

As the worst thing in Dinamo this season Denis cites bad energy. He thinks it is caused by bad moves inside the club. He judges that the **transfer window was done catastrophically**. He says that a person with power, contacts and resources like Zvonimir Boban cannot afford such a transfer window in crucial positions. He also reproaches the bringing in of „almost all clumsy players”, the not bringing in of a goalkeeper and the not giving of a chance, which are already old topics.

Denis connects this with Boban's position. Boban, in his opinion, got into some kind of "mad masochism" around the stadium. He thinks it naive to expect that a tangle of negative energy, not only around the coach but around the entire management, will not be reflected on the team. Last year Kovačević had behind him the stable figure of Zvonimir Boban and maximum authority in carrying out decisions. Today neither players nor fans are firmly behind him, so Kovačević no longer swims as before. Denis warns that players are "the most popular commodity in the world".

The opening part of the season can still serve as an excuse, but not forever. Denis repeats that he sees no sense in avoiding big cuts. He also stresses that, with Hajduk and Rijeka like this, Dinamo would have to be champion for the question to be closed at all.

sections.subtitle: Europe Is Not a Luxury: The Club's Budget Depends on Success on the Continent
sections.screenshot_description: Denis explains why Europe is a priority and the foundation of Dinamo's budget
sections.content:
Profa asks whether Denis is worried about the title or about Europe, noting that the title is for now not the main concern. Denis answers that he does not know where the idea comes from that Europe is not the most important pillar of the club's long-term stability. According to him, Europe is the priority both last year and this year. A Dinamo that will not play the Europa League has achieved the minimum of minimums, but it needs to play, and successfully.

He explains the link between European success and finances:

- if Dinamo does not play successfully in Europe, there are no player sales,
- without sales nobody can fulfil the budget,
- the long-term strategy must include giving a chance to young people, and then foreigners should not be the only solution either.

Denis adds that it is precisely that way that the club, with a lot of money "thrown to the wind", burned the bridge towards the future. If the strategy is long-term, he says, then nobody would have anything to reproach it for.

sections.subtitle: Hajduk's First Goal and the Lack of a Plan B Without Mišić
sections.screenshot_description: Analysis of Hajduk's first goal and a conversation about play without Mišić
sections.content:
The conversation then returns to the derby itself and Hajduk's first goal. Denis describes it as a combination of circumstances. Maračić made a block on one Dinamo player, which according to Denis was certainly a tactical idea of aggressiveness at that set piece, and for that he gives him every credit. The ball then passed to the Hajduk player who shot from that angle and, according to Denis's words, did not even see the ball at all. Denis calls this an unlucky circumstance. Profa notes that Šimun Hrgović's ball that preceded the situation was excellent.

Denis calls the absence of Josip Mišić an already told story. He says Dinamo without him looks boring, and on paper has not managed to win a single match in which it could not use what he gives it. He thinks one could have gone with another formation, especially in Split, in unusual circumstances and without Stojković and Mišić. Insisting on the same postulates as when all the settings are different, he says, is **football suicide**. He sees no sense in Dinamo functioning all the time in a 4-3-3 system, while not trying to surprise with anything.

Profa agrees and describes how Dinamo tried to replace Mišić. There was no attempt at opening the play through the middle, rather they were mostly long balls from the back line. He does not blame an individual, but the organization of play, because no attempt at all was made to replace Mišić. Denis concludes: Dinamo made a copy of Mišić instead of making a new model for the situation in which he is absent.

sections.subtitle: Missed Preparation and the Question of the Right Back
sections.screenshot_description: Denis and Profa discuss the starting lineup and the player at right back
sections.content:
Profa asks Denis whether, when he saw the lineup, he expected 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3 and admits that he himself thought it would be 4-2-3-1. Denis answers that this would have been a more desirable change than what was seen. His assessment is: **missed lineup, missed match preparation** and Garcia took the win in everything. He adds that it is not difficult to prepare for Dinamo, because everyone knows what and how it will play. If Dinamo is not markedly dominant or energetically good, it is no advantage even against Lokomotiva, and all coaches know how to play against it.

Profa also talks about Bamba. He notes that he is not Dinamo's biggest problem and that everything he did he did via the side on which he played. But he thinks his movements in attack were also deficient.

Most of the discussion is about the right back. Profa stresses that the coach's stubbornness bothers him when it comes to that player and mentions how the coach justified the decision after the match. He additionally emphasized that he will not play with three centre-backs, although Galešić has several times played as a "third centre-back", that is, right back.

Denis has not won the league as a coach nor does he have a licence, but he thinks he can judge that **Tadinac in quality does not match Dinamo's team and demands**, especially in big matches. He stresses that he is a player for situations when the opponent defends in a low block and when his explosiveness and occasional good cross can come to the fore. He is not a young player and has no sales potential. He also reasons that, if Dinamo cannot produce a right back, then it can shut down the school. Of Galešić he says that he proved he can play in that position, and yet does not get a chance. Because of this he sees only two possible explanations: the decision was imposed on the coach or the coach is "lost". A third scenario, according to him, does not exist.

Profa notes that Tadinac looked fine against Lokomotiva, and Denis responds that scouting is what worries him. It surprises him even more that the player ends up in the starting lineup in important matches.

sections.subtitle: Dominguez's Credit and the Coach Who Leads Scouts
sections.screenshot_description: Denis criticizes Dominguez's status and the coach's lack of self-criticism
sections.content:
The conversation then moves to the centre-back pair and Hajduk's equalizing goal, which came after a foul. Profa and Denis judge that both Dominguez and the other centre-back played bad matches. Profa recalls that, in his opinion, the coach after the match practically admitted everything that is wrong, including the changes.

Denis does not understand on what basis Dominguez has such credit. Dinamo has perhaps the greatest breadth in quality precisely in the centre-back positions, with Galešić and Radeljić, that is, four very good centre-backs. Dominguez, according to him, made over ten direct errors in important matches at a high level. Despite that he still has "crazy credit" with Kovačević. Denis describes this as believing in the wrong players.

He particularly misses the **self-criticism** of Dinamo's coach after the match and towards the players. All of that, he says, seems as if he leads scouts: after the match comes the message that next weekend it will be better. „Dinamo can't do that”, he concludes.

Profa also mentions Kovačević's statement that he cannot reproach the players for anything. He adds that the coach said he would go mad if he once heard that, but he is not sure whether he said it immediately after the match.

sections.subtitle: Praise for Hajduk: A Good Match Without a Bunker
sections.screenshot_description: Profa reads a greeting from viewer Ana Lovrić and comments on Hajduk's play
sections.content:
In the middle of the conversation Denis warns Profa that a message from viewer Ana Lovrić has arrived. Profa answers her with a greeting and reads her comment: she wants to praise her Hajduk, which after so many years did not defend itself and did not stand in a block against Dinamo.

Denis agrees with the content of the message and judges that Hajduk played a good match. He describes the first half as even. He admits that Hajduk was slightly better to him and with greater initiative, but agrees that it was 50:50. In the second half, after the initial minutes while regular conditions still prevailed, Hajduk was, according to him, much better. He adds that Dinamo did not show desire in the fight for second balls and that Hajduk's players "beat them up".

Profa praises Hajduk's positioning in the middle of the pitch, because of which its players always looked closer to the ball, and mentions that Luka spoke well about second balls. He stresses that he does not want to underestimate Hajduk, but when he sees those players, he does not want to even remember them, regardless of the number of foreigners and of the fact that they once mocked Dinamo. He adds that this season Hajduk's results have been changeable: Hajduk lost at Rujevica to Rijeka 1:0, and coach Garcia to this day has not won a single derby.

Denis says that Bamba was not just good, but dominated, and Profa defends him to some extent. He describes him as a player who, when he looks good, looks super, and when he does not look good, then he does not look good. Denis perceives him as a player without technique. Profa notes that Hajduk's Krakow is last in the league, and Denis concludes that Dinamo should not respect so much either Hajduk's numbers or its team.

sections.subtitle: Criticism Without Personal Attacks and the Mystery of the Wingers in 4-3-3
sections.screenshot_description: Profa and Denis discuss the role of the wingers in the 4-3-3 system
sections.content:
Denis warns that reactions to a defeat must be balanced towards the players and the coach. He agrees that one must not attack on a personal level. He criticizes social networks, on which, he says, more and more criticism relates to non-football reasons, to the coach, the president and others. Such criticism becomes meaningless and moves away from what happens on the pitch. He adds that before some matches a curtain was noticed that protected people in the club, which is now too weak.

Profa then opens the topic of the 4-3-3 system. He recalls that it maximizes the chance for the wingers and asks what the wingers did in the derby. Denis answers: nothing. As a big mistake he cites that the engine of the play does not enter the corridor, and even in secondary roles the players did not show the tactical knowledge that would be expected.

Denis presents how he would put the team together. In the eight position **Ivan Sušec** would play instead of Zajec. On the left he would go with his own choice, and he would give a chance to Hodžić. On the right side Franjo Topić or Alen would play.

Profa mentions a viewer's comment that Ivanišević and Almeida both like to come into the centre and so do not give width. Denis rejects this: he has never heard that a left winger cannot play on the right or vice versa, and calls it the greatest stupidity he has heard in modern football analysis. He also mentions that Ivanišević was brought in as an eight, and today was one of the more dangerous in attack, although Denis in the end agreed that he did not play in that position.

sections.subtitle: Zajec's Drop in Form and Praise for Individuals
sections.screenshot_description: Profa asks Denis about Niko Zajec's drop, and Denis praises Belje
sections.content:
Profa asks Denis how he views Niko Zajec's drastic drop this season. Denis says he does not know what exactly is wrong, but recalls that last season Zajec was, along with Stojković, the best footballer in the league. If an MVP award were handed out, he sees both names among the main candidates.

Then he praises Belje, whom he describes as a positive surprise. What he did last season he continues this season too, and Denis sees that he is ready to do it continuously. He states that last season he scored over 20 goals in the HNL, and compares him with Duje Čop, who once scored over 20 goals, but is not a player who can repeat that from season to season. About Belje he says he deserves every credit and that today he would not reproach him for anything in particular.

Profa agrees that Belje was by far Dinamo's best player and adds praise, although he had problems with digestion. He also mentions that one goal was the result of a big error, but Denis does not consider it decisive. Profa repeats that Hajduk's first goal seemed funny to him.

sections.subtitle: What Is 4-3-3 For in Dinamo? Salaries, Money and the Question of Sense
sections.screenshot_description: Denis asks whether it makes sense for Dinamo to play 4-3-3 and talks about thrown-away money
sections.content:
Denis stresses a question that, as he says, has been nagging him for all five months. It is asked by „many people” who are coaches: is there any football logic for a team like Dinamo to play 4-3-3 with the first team, like the best teams in the history of football, among which he mentions Barcelona. He claims that he has not heard anyone say that it makes sense.

He explains when this system would make sense: when Dinamo would not have to be a club chasing the champion's title. Then, he says, a club like Istra would do it, for which it is all the same whether it will be third or eighth, and the main goal is for players from the juniors to move easily into the seniors and to be sold. Such a system helps sales, because it is easier to sell players who play 4-3-3 and to buy players for that system. But Dinamo has other goals: to be good in Europe, to win the title and in that way to fill the budget.

Here Denis also mentions thrown-away money. He finds it unbelievable how much money has been thrown to the wind, and at the same time stresses that the lost derby shows that Dinamo is not better even when the players have experience.

Denis also poses a question to the players. Their names and salaries should be studied before they say whether they are what Dinamo needs. He asks whether players like Mišić could play constantly in that system or should have raised their voice, and given the coach more freedom to try something else, especially in derbies and European matches.

sections.subtitle: Rain as an Alibi and the Psychology of the Derby
sections.screenshot_description: Denis and Profa talk about the irregular conditions at Poljud
sections.content:
Denis ironizes one of the alibis, the rain and the pitch. He stresses that, while the pitch was in an almost water-polo state, Hajduk's players looked much better, but Dinamo created the most danger precisely then. He says: "We created the most danger while there were irregular conditions."

Profa adds that psychologically Hajduk was also better because Dinamo withdrew. Denis thinks the missed chance was big because a goal at that moment, in his assessment, would have extinguished Hajduk for the whole season. Profa follows up that then, if Dinamo had scored, Dinamo's player would still be „Mister Derby”.

Denis links this with the general problem with people who praise or condemn according to current form. He thinks that a tendency of bad results gives birth to criticism that crosses the line, and when "everyone is booting him", there is nothing special to say. He stresses that everyone sees that this story is going towards its end. The only question is how long it will last and whether there will be a surprising twist in which the dressing room shows that it is with the coach. For such a possibility there is for now nothing he could hold onto.

sections.subtitle: Is Kovačević Still for Dinamo? Guardiola, Klopp and Tied Hands
sections.screenshot_description: Profa and Denis talk about Kovačević's future on Dinamo's bench
sections.content:
Profa stresses that it bothers him that individuals have criticized Kovačević from the start, but that does not mean they are right now. He emphasizes that it is hard to be Dinamo's coach, and especially to be so for long.

Denis cites the example of Pep Guardiola, who finished one season with City in fourth place, and the next was even stronger. He thinks that sport is not mathematics. Processes sometimes come to an end, circumstances change and energy is lost, so he returns to the comparison with a couple who separate although both are still „top”. Profa adds the example of Klopp, who with Borussia Dortmund in the last season almost dropped out of the league.

Profa thinks it stupid to reduce everything to the question of whether Kovačević is for Dinamo or not. He achieved the goals, and the question is how many coaches in one stretch did fewer matches than him. Denis agrees: when he delivered the half-season and fulfilled the goals, he is obviously for Dinamo, but that does not mean that he has to be forever.

Denis gives him a chance too: what bothers him most is that Kovačević **never actually got a chance in Dinamo**. It was never possible to see the full scope of his coaching potential, because, according to Denis, he had his hands tied the whole time in terms of creation. Profa notes that someone could say that this is precisely why he was brought in. Denis responds that there is no reason at all for a coach not to accept such an offer and that it was a chance he had to accept. The key question for him is how to turn the situation around. If Dinamo loses to Anderlecht, then another match in Europe and one in the HNL, he does not know what could be. He also asks who could be the next coach and to whom a chance could be given.

sections.subtitle: The Substitutions Were a Symptom, Not the Cause
sections.screenshot_description: Profa comments on the coach's statements after the match about the prepared substitutions
sections.content:
Profa looks back at the statements after the match. Kovačević said that the substitutions had been prepared, but Profa thinks that this remained unfinished: on the one hand he said that they went in too late, and on the other that the players were ready, so the question is whether that is his fault. He asks what kind of explanation that is. He adds that, in his opinion, it also happened to Bilić that more than half of Croatia saw the need for a change at the moment when Spain scored the equalizing goal.

Denis, however, does not consider the statements decisive. He says the substitutions were not a problem for him. **The problem was the match preparation and the starting eleven.** He does not think that the substitutions, if they had been a few minutes earlier or later, would have changed anything important. He agrees with Profa that the whole process was problematic, but the substitutions are only a consequence of the bad initial plan.

sections.subtitle: Refereeing, Yellow and Red Card: Dinamo Must Not Look for the Culprit in the Referee
sections.screenshot_description: Denis and Profa comment on the disputed situations and the cards
sections.content:
Denis decisively does not want to highlight the refereeing as a reason for the defeat. He judges the refereeing bad, but thinks that Hajduk, if it had not won, would have been "breathing fire" because of the yellow cards. He claims it is unbelievable that yellow cards do not touch some Dinamo players, and asks who would get away without a card for such fouls and unsporting actions. If the referee lets it go, the player later brings himself into trouble. He also criticizes referees who constantly explain decisions to players, a minute and a half to two minutes per intervention. He thinks the referee should judge the foul and give a yellow card or not explain.

Denis, on the basis of watching on a mobile phone without multiple angles, says that in the disputed situation he saw a **red card**. Profa agrees, especially given the pitch and the carelessness of the tackle, and besides thinks ridiculous those who say the player should have received two yellow cards, because things do not work that way. When he saw the tackle, he immediately thought of a red card. Profa describes that he thought that he would „go off” and that Dinamo had got away with it, and was bad. He mentions that the player kicked the ball away and then tackled.

Profa then comments on the derby statistics. The eternal quarrel over who is the bigger thief and over refereeing and salaries is ridiculous to him, given that the same referee refereed the eighth derby, and in the derbies so far five wins for Hajduk and three draws have been achieved, if he is not mistaken. Denis adds that even before the match he told Luka that whoever loses, the referee will be to blame. He cannot believe that among Dinamo's fans the focus too is on the referees, and there are ten objective reasons for the defeat that should not be obscured. Profa adds that, as far as the broader picture is concerned, he believes that Hajduk nevertheless has higher salaries, but does not consider that relevant for this match. With that he closes the discussion about refereeing at the very end of this part of the conversation.

iterations.theme: Jokes, viewers' questions, foreign referees, Kovačević until Anderlecht and announcement of the rest of the trip

sections.subtitle: Three Scarves for One Fan: Souvenirs, Ronaldo and Jokes at Profa's Expense
sections.screenshot_description: Profa and Denis joke while showing purchased souvenirs with the image of Cristiano Ronaldo
sections.content:
After a serious discussion about refereeing, Dinamo and the derby, the conversation in the 44th minute abruptly opens into a more relaxed tone. Denis asks Profa to show what souvenir he bought, and Profa answers that he has more than one, mentioning that all three items from his list ended up in the bag. Denis then quips: „Look at Ronaldo“, which begins a series of jokes at the expense of Profa's love for Cristiano Ronaldo.

The two hosts exchange lines, and the conversation at moments turns into an improvised sketch. Profa then recalls that during the day they were in the National Football Museum, and Denis quips about the enormous representation of Cristiano Ronaldo among the exhibits. The tone is clearly humorous, without more serious analysis: after a tense derby and a long day in England, the duo gives itself over to humour.

The hint of the souvenir returns to the episode later too: Denis will in one joke mention that it is hard to take seriously someone who wears around the neck **three scarves of Cristiano Ronaldo**.

sections.subtitle: Football Museum and Old Trafford: Two Favourite Pictures in One Place
sections.screenshot_description: Profa enthusiastically retells the visit to the National Football Museum and Old Trafford
sections.content:
Profa explains that that day they visited the **National Football Museum**, and then Old Trafford. It was there, he says, that he felt happiest since arriving in England, despite Dinamo's defeat that was still weighing on him.

As soon as he got out of the taxi, he saw the first picture, on which, as he describes, were **two of his biggest favourites in the same photograph**: Cristiano's goal against Portsmouth, the well-known rocket, and **Niko Kranjčar in the wall**, over whom the ball indeed passed. At that scene, says Profa, he was very happy, and he is generally satisfied by how much Ronaldo is represented in that place.

The satisfaction was brief: Profa then looked for items with Ronaldo's image that did not greet him on the shelf. An employee explained to him that the goods were sold out (*sold out*). When he finally managed to get what he was looking for, he decided to send a greeting to the group he calls „Sportivo 7 Club“.

sections.subtitle: Viewer's Question: Why Does Dinamo Play Worse Than Last Season?
sections.screenshot_description: Profa reads a viewer's question about the main reason for Dinamo's weaker play
sections.content:
The hosts move on to viewers' questions. Profa reads one of them, which asks what in their opinion is the **main reason why Dinamo plays worse than last season**. Denis adds to this that one of the commenters, Šašek, wrote that the podcast has only „paid comments“, and Profa takes that with a joke. Denis also adds that in England, given the prices, „20 pounds“ seems like a good day.

When the conversation gets to the essence, Profa says that what first comes to mind is **saturation with the coach**. He adds that this is his first impression, and that behind it also stands a **bad transfer window**.

As the third element he cites **disappointment after Viking**, that is, the psychological component. He admits that he, as an emotional fan, needed a long time to recover after the match in Stavanger. He concludes that he would recover faster from a shipwreck than from that European defeat.

sections.subtitle: Denis: Energy Spilled from the Top onto the Coach, and the Transfer Window Was One of the Worse Ones
sections.screenshot_description: Denis explains how bad energy was transferred from the top of the club to the players
sections.content:
Denis also answers the same question. As the main reason he cites **the change of energy in the club**. In his opinion, everything that was happening at the top of the club spilled onto the coach's back, and the players felt it. He says they are „a bit shaken“ and that all this culminated in such play.

Denis says clearly that it is understandable to him why it is avoided to admit that Dinamo **did a very bad transfer window**, one of the worse in recent times. He thinks the team is because of this weaker than in previous seasons.

In this part of the conversation there is also a short comment about a young player who came on from the bench during the match and, in Denis's impression, left a good impression, but the recording in this part is not entirely clear, so details remain undefined.

sections.subtitle: English Food and a Ban on Foreign Referees: Denis Demands Domestic Referees at Every Match
sections.screenshot_description: Denis comments with disapproval on English food, and then discusses foreign referees
sections.content:
A question about England opens the topic of food, and Denis does not spare words: „I have no bigger crap than English food.“ What especially bothered him was **beans for breakfast**, and the impression of the dishes they tried he describes as „really impossible“. Profa joins the joke, with a comment that things looked „terrible“ to him.

Then the conversation moves to **foreign referees**. Denis says he would ban them by decree in Croatian football and insists that domestic referees referee at every match. He thinks the only way for domestic referees to progress is for them to be given a chance, even at derbies. He wonders when domestic referees will „finally come onto the scene“ and who will ever take them if the most important matches are not given.

Profa takes the opposite stance: given Hajduk's matches so far, against Hajduk he would nevertheless put foreign referees. Denis at this stresses that Croatia is not „savagery like Greece or Turkey“ and that the country should be able to have a normal system of referee organization. He concludes the debate with the question what kind of football association is one that does not manage to develop referees.

sections.subtitle: Six Foreigners in the Starting Eleven: Is Kovačević–Dinamo a Worn-Out Story?
sections.screenshot_description: The hosts discuss Hajduk's foreign players and the relationship between Kovačević and Dinamo
sections.content:
Profa reads a question from a viewer, signed as „second ball“, who asks how a team with Spaniards, Swedes and Filipinos can function. Profa links this topic with Hajduk, noting that Hajduk that day had **six foreigners in the starting eleven**.

Denis does not consider that an important argument: in the world of football there are many examples in which teams with more different nationalities function flawlessly. The question, he thinks, is not in foreigners, but in relationships inside the club.

Here he moves to Kovačević. Denis thinks that last year he proved that he **can work with Dinamo**, but that the relationships wore out over time. He stresses that this is not a personal blow to the coach, nor to his coaching knowledge: „I think that it is a worn-out story between Kovačević and Dinamo.“

sections.subtitle: Only One Away Win: Dinamo's European and Domestic Away Record
sections.screenshot_description: Profa and Denis count Dinamo's away wins this season
sections.content:
Profa asks how many away wins Dinamo has this season. Denis first answers that it is **only one**, and that against Žalgiris. Profa doubts, so the two hosts together recall the schedule and results.

Profa recalls that Dinamo visited Istra, Osijek and Hajduk, and Denis adds the European matches against Viking and Hapoel from Beer Shave. According to Denis, apart from Žalgiris there is not a single other away win in official matches. The conversation is interspersed with interjections and corrections, so it is not entirely clear which matches they counted as away.

Still, Denis stresses one thing: Viking and Hapoel were teams that, in his judgment, were **weaker than Dinamo**, which further emphasizes the disappointment with such away form.

sections.subtitle: Hajduk Comments on YouTube and the Question of Who Actually Dominated in Derbies
sections.screenshot_description: Profa reads Hajduk comments under the video while Denis comments on them
sections.content:
Profa reads viewers' comments, among them one signed as Zoki, in which a Hajduk fan announces that his club will be champion. Denis to this ironically says that he feels „fear of the domination of the Hajduk kužina on YouTube“.

Profa also reads a comment that relies on the fact that Dinamo has not won at Maksimir „1000 days“. Profa questions this and claims that Hajduk has not beaten them for **678 days**, after which he tries to count when Hajduk last won in an important match. The answer, he says, refers to almost the „last millennium“, so the entire commentator's argument is illogical to him.

Denis accepts this as a joke. He says he feels anger, but cannot take it seriously. In addition he adds that three times messages reached him about an alleged throwing of a flare towards disabled people, but that he did not see or hear it and does not know whether it is true, so he does not want to comment.

sections.subtitle: The Podcast Under the Magnifying Glass: Viewership, Small and Big Podcasts and the Promise of 10,000 Followers
sections.screenshot_description: The hosts and an interlocutor read questions about viewership and the future of the podcast
sections.content:
One of the interlocutors reads a question referring to the show itself: how can Denis be a guest on podcasts when, if the viewership is not large, it could be a waste of time. The question is formulated unclearly in the conversation, but Profa judges it a good one.

Denis answers that he should in fact appear only on big podcasts, but „big podcasts don't call me“. Therefore, he says, he goes to **smaller, almost boutique podcasts**.

Profa in addition adds that he sees his interlocutors as friends and invites people to follow the podcast **8_24** and congratulates on the questions. Denis hopes that one day they will reach ten thousand followers. A question from viewer Mario that Profa received via message is also mentioned. Most of the conversation in this part is humorous, with many interjections and improvised lines.

sections.subtitle: Should Kovačević Stay At Least Until Anderlecht? Profa: Let It Be His Last Exam
sections.screenshot_description: Profa explains his position on Kovačević staying until the match with Anderlecht
sections.content:
Profa recalls a conversation from the time after the match with Hapoel, when someone posed the question what if Kovačević loses at Poljud. Profa says that he then objectively answered that in that case he would no longer defend the coach. The defeat, of course, happened.

When the question is posed what now, Profa takes a more conciliatory stance: if anything is in question, **Kovačević should stay until the match with Anderlecht**. If Boban or someone else is not sure of his decision, let it be seen what will happen in that match.

Profa notes that shock therapy, that is, the dismissal of the coach, **is not a guarantee that Dinamo will beat Anderlecht**. Therefore, he concludes, it is best that the match with Anderlecht be „truly the last exam“ for him.

sections.subtitle: Dinamo's Beginnings: Vlado Novak, an Ad in Večernji list and the Generation of '91
sections.screenshot_description: Denis tells how as a six-year-old he entered Dinamo's football school
sections.content:
To a viewer's question who was his first coach at Dinamo, Denis answers that it was **Vlado Novak**. He remembers that it was an open school of Dinamo, and the story begins with an ad in *Večernji list*.

Denis was then six and a half years old. His grandmother bought that paper, and he, as he says, could already read. He saw an ad that invited children to enrol in Dinamo, and then took it to his parents.

Vlado Novak, says Denis, was the first coach in the 91 generation, in which **Kramarić** also was. The generation, he says, was not particularly successful, but Kramarić made the most of all of them. Novak, he adds, was a „great man“ and an excellent coach for working with children.

Profa in addition jokes that *Večernji* also carried coupons for winnings. Denis also mentions Davor Blašković, whom he describes as another coach who was connected with Dinamo.

sections.subtitle: Prize Questions and Impressions of England: Architecture Yes, Weather No, Homeless People Worrying
sections.screenshot_description: The hosts talk about a prize question and their impressions of England
sections.content:
Profa recalls that he is obliged to hand out **three prizes** for the prize questions and that people will „kill“ him if he does not, which implies an additional prize as well. The conversation then moves to how England impressed them.

Denis poses the question whether England is **overrated** outside football, with a note that they perhaps do not have a large enough sample for such a judgment. Profa says that the weather is nice for him that day, that he likes the **architecture** very much and that a brick stadium would also please him. He adds that it is clear to him why someone goes to Madrid because of the weather.

What most surprised Denis in England was the **number of homeless people**. Profa then also mentions that in Brussels they were dissatisfied because of the price increase of tuition fees and other costs, but this part of the conversation remains unfinished.

sections.subtitle: Tomorrow Hull – Everton: What the Hosts Expect and Why Hull Is Not Huddersfield
sections.screenshot_description: Profa and Denis announce tomorrow's Hull – Everton match and future episodes
sections.content:
Profa asks whether there are more smart questions, and then announces that at the end he will say what they expect from tomorrow. An interlocutor notes that some questions repeat, and Denis again comments on the number of the podcast's followers.

Profa announces that an episode recorded **at a table**, in the old „old school“ style, with Denis and him as main speakers, will follow soon, but for that conditions need to be secured.

Denis then announces tomorrow's match: it is interesting to him that **Hull** is a club different from Huddersfield and that this is a big enigma to them. He describes the Hull – Everton match as a reward for their „karma“, and mentions that he bought an Everton flag. Profa jokingly adds that, if Hull loses, he will be in „heavy deficit“, and then states that they are about halfway through this adventure.

sections.subtitle: Expensive England: 50 Pounds a Day Is Not Enough, and a Ticket for United – Tottenham 80 Pounds
sections.screenshot_description: The hosts compare the prices of travel, transport and tickets in England
sections.content:
Denis stresses that in England **everything is extremely expensive**. He estimates that 50 pounds a day is not enough to get through the day, and when public transport, taxi or train is counted in, costs rise further.

Profa talks about his ticket for the match **United – Tottenham** at Old Trafford, which he bought the day before the match. There were tickets for **80 pounds**, but with the condition that club membership is also bought. It surprises him that for a match of such rank there were still seats only two days earlier, as well as the price itself.

The example shows how financially demanding everyday football tourism in England is, and the hosts joke and discuss how much such a ticket would cost within Croatian frameworks.

sections.subtitle: Agreement on the Continuation: Video Instead of Podcast if the Internet Fails
sections.screenshot_description: Profa and Denis agree how they will record the continuation if Hull wins
sections.content:
Profa proposes a simple agreement: **if Hull wins tomorrow, they will get in touch** with new content. Denis interjects that the internet is bad everywhere, to which Profa replies that they can simply **record a video and upload it afterwards**.

Denis jokingly proposes a „tactical analysis of Hall by positions“, and Profa accepts the idea that they conclude everything in a „victorious“ tone. He then announces that he will leave the closing word to Denis, although he will nevertheless end the conversation.

The agreement thus remains loose and relaxed, but clear: the continuation of the trip will be documented, and the form depends on the result and technical conditions.

sections.subtitle: Denis's Closing Word: The Pressure Is on Hajduk, and the Title Must Not Be Lost
sections.screenshot_description: Denis gives a closing message about the pressure on Hajduk because of the fight for the title
sections.content:
In the closing word Denis turns the perspective: after the derby the pressure, he claims, shifts to Hajduk. If Hajduk **loses the title** to such a Dinamo, he says, it will „burn everything“, because it will no longer have any excuses. Profa answers him that „the little ball is on you“.

There follow several minutes of a humorous attempt to record the closing message into the camera, with Denis's interjections and Profa's confused attempt to turn the phone. At one point they joke at the expense of a „young bachelor of 34 years“ and mention wet clothes after the rain. Denis then invites listeners not to waste time on smaller projects, but to watch the reruns on the podcast's channel.

He also announces that tomorrow he will publish Profa's interview to the English media.

sections.subtitle: Profa's Review of Jakir's Statement and Conclusion: We Took Over England, We Continue On
sections.screenshot_description: Profa comments on the media transmission of Jakir's statement near the end of the podcast
sections.content:
Shortly before the end Profa asks for the floor because, as he says, he still has to say something. He believes that most viewers saw the day before **Jakir's statement**, published through the club, but it angered him how one sports portal conveyed it. He states that in *Sportske novosti* they conveyed the story, and that at the end of the press conference he was asked a question about the Croatian derby.

Profa ironizes that it is about a „man who is currently the happiest on Šolta“, concluding that there is nothing interesting in all of it.

The conclusion of the conversation is short and humorous: „We took over England and we continue on.“ Profa once more recalls Denis's words, that **the little ball is on Hajduk's side** and that they can only lose the title themselves.
